title: Freya and the Garden
premise: Ulyana Pemberton carves bones into charms for the dead in Thornmere Valley, a sanctuary where magic cannot cross the boundary stones — until the old gods, long silent, begin answering prayers again and drag her voice into their war. Guided by Freya, a forgotten goddess bound into the body of a garden warden, Ulyana must leave the valley that has protected her all her life and reforge the broken covenant between gods and mortals before an endless winter swallows both realms. Betrayed by the loyal friend who silenced the gods to save her own family, Ulyana learns that truth costs more than loyalty ever did. In the end she sacrifices her hearing — the gift of the dead — to seal the new covenant, choosing a quiet life with Freya over the voices she has always known.
about_author: Sable Okonkwo is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist turned novelist who writes about grief, memory, and the small magics of ordinary hands. They live beside a botanical garden where they claim the flowers gossip after dark.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ulyana Pemberton carves a memorial bone for a drowned child, hearing his last words as she works. Her valley forbids magic, yet her gift persists at its edges. When a prayer she never spoke is answered aloud, she realizes something old has woken. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: lonely competence cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Bean Rows
chapters.summary: Following the answered prayer to the overgrown shrine-garden on her grandmother's land, Ulyana meets Freya, a woman who tends beans by day and remembers being a goddess by night. Freya claims the covenant binding gods from mortals was shattered deliberately. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: wary fascination; two isolated beings recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana tests Freya's story against the dead themselves, questioning the oldest skull in her workshop. The dead confirm: the gods were not banished but muted, and someone mortal helped do it. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread replacing skepticism; her craft becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Boundary Stones
chapters.summary: Freya shows Ulyana the boundary stones and explains why magic cannot follow her inside: the valley is a wound where the covenant was cut. Beyond it, winter has already begun falling out of season. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: homesickness for divinity; guilt over what godhood cost mortals.

chapters.title: Marta's Silence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's closest friend Marta grows evasive when asked about the valley's founding families. That night Ulyana hears a dead man whisper Marta's grandmother's name alongside the word 'muted.' POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: first fracture of trust; loyalty beginning to war with truth.

chapters.title: First Frost in High Summer
chapters.summary: Frost kills the midsummer market crops. Refugees arrive claiming the world beyond the stones is freezing solid, and prayers are being answered with cruel literalism by half-remembered gods. The elders demand answers Ulyana cannot safely give. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: community panic; the personal becoming public.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: A traveling mapmaker named Ivo offers to guide Ulyana past the boundary stones, owing a debt to her late mother. Freya warns the road is watched by the Hollow Choir — gods gone feral from silence. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: reluctant courage; leaving home means grieving it in advance.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Ulyana steps beyond the stones for the first time and is flooded by every dead voice within miles — overwhelming, ecstatic, terrible. Freya anchors her, and their bond deepens into something tender and unspoken. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: sensory overwhelm transformed into intimacy.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: The trio is ambushed by the Hollow Choir, gods who wear frozen faces and sing prayers back at their askers. Freya fights them off using Ulyana's carved charms as vessels, revealing how much power a mortal's craft can hold. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: terror and awe; love expressed through protection.

chapters.title: The God Who Kept His Name
chapters.summary: They shelter with Torvald, a hearth-god who refused muting and burned his own temples to stay free. He reveals the covenant can be reforged only at the Worldroot, using a mortal voice that hears the dead and a god who remembers her name. POV: Torvald. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag attached.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Ivo confesses he was paid to lead them into the Hollow Choir's path — by someone in Thornmere. Ulyana recognizes the seal: Marta's family crest. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve; loyalty formally broken.

chapters.title: The Muting
chapters.summary: In a vision through the bones, Ulyana witnesses the original muting: Marta's grandmother led the valley elders in cutting the covenant to hide a plague the gods refused to cure. Truth and loyalty become indistinguishable wounds. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief for a friend and a homeland built on a lie.

chapters.title: Winter's Teeth
chapters.summary: The party crosses the frozen Ashfall Reach as the long winter accelerates. Ivo loses fingers to frostbite saving the charm-bag, and Ulyana realizes the winter is not weather but the covenant dying — realms unraveling together. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: sacrifice without heroics; endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: The City of Answered Prayers
chapters.summary: They reach Vaskr, where desperate crowds worship wildly specific gods born overnight from panicked wishes. Freya sees her possible future: to be remembered wrongly is worse than being forgotten. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: identity horror; what survives of a self when others define it.

chapters.title: Marta at the Gate
chapters.summary: Marta intercepts them at Vaskr's gate, sent by the valley elders to bring Ulyana home. She admits her family's role in the muting and begs Ulyana to let the old gods die quietly rather than risk everything. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: love weaponized as caution; apology without absolution.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes
chapters.summary: Ulyana must choose: return with Marta to a valley that will freeze anyway, or finish the road. She chooses truth, and Marta — shattered — chooses to follow her instead of stopping her. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: reconciliation without forgiveness; loyalty reborn on honest terms.

chapters.title: Descent to the Worldroot
chapters.summary: Guided by Torvald's last ember, they descend beneath the roots of the first tree, where the severed halves of the covenant hang like a snapped bridge. The Hollow Choir waits below, singing Ulyana's own name. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Choir's Bargain
chapters.summary: The Hollow Choir offers Ulyana a bargain: restore the old covenant exactly, restoring the muting too, and everyone lives comfortably in silence forever. Freya refuses on her behalf before Ulyana can answer — and Ulyana is furious at being spoken for. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: love's arrogance confronted; the cost of protection.

chapters.title: Reforge
chapters.summary: At the Worldroot, Ulyana begins carving the new covenant into living bone while Freya speaks her true name into it. The Hollow Choir attacks; Marta and Ivo hold the line. To complete the work, Ulyana must give up the sense that defines her. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: climax — choice made in full knowledge of loss.

chapters.title: The Quiet After
chapters.summary: Ulyana seals the covenant and goes deaf to the dead forever, collapsing into Freya's arms as spring floods the roots. The Hollow Choir dissolves into remembered names, mourned rather than destroyed. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief and relief entangled; silence as peace, not absence.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: They return to Thornmere as the thaw begins. The elders confront their history publicly; Marta stands beside Ulyana as witness, not defender. Ulyana keeps carving bones, now purely art, and plants Freya's garden inside the boundary stones. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: bittersweet restoration; home remade honestly.

chapters.title: Freya and the Garden
chapters.summary: One year later, Freya tends a garden that now grows things from both realms, and Ulyana has learned to read lips, laughter, and Freya's hands instead of ghosts. A child asks if the dead still talk to the bone-carver. 'No,' Ulyana says, taking Freya's hand. 'I finally learned to listen to the living.' POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: resolution — love chosen over memory, and memory honored anyway.
